PART 3
[8 marks]
[Time suggested: Twenty minutes]
Questions 19 to 26 are based on the following passage.
Read the passage carefully and choose the best answer A, B, C or D. For each question,
mark your answer on the answer sheet.
If you ask people to pick their choice of the greatest invention in the field of
communication technology, most of them will pick the internet. It’s surprising to know
that in the 1990s, not many people had even heard of it, let alone had access to it, but,
as of 2021, more than 59% of the world’s population has got the access.
The internet is a network of networks that connects millions of computers across the
world. Specifically, it’s a group of networks that consists of government, private sector,
university, and business networks that are linked by wireless, optical, and electronic
technologies.
There are many reasons why the internet is a source of entertainment. It offers a lot of
free online games to play as well as websites that allow you to watch movies, TV series,
and videos, and listen to music for free. Besides, there are chat rooms and forums that
give you the chance to chat, discuss, and share ideas with others.
Next, the internet can keep you well informed of what’s happening around the world.
You can read about current news or find out about the latest developments in
governments, politics, sports, major events, or festivals taking place in even the most
remote places in the world. Likewise, it gives businesses a platform to advertise their
wares. You can do comparison shopping easily and search for the products and services
that meet your needs without having to visit numerous brick-and-mortar stores.
Lastly, the internet makes shopping online possible. There are thousands of virtual
stores offering a wide selection of products, and the number is increasing every year.
The internet has revolutionised shopping and kicked off an entirely new way of selling
and shopping. At the same time, it has allowed many people to start their small
businesses to sell their homegrown products.
On the other hand, the internet has several drawbacks that we cannot ignore. First, it
isn’t a safe place for children and young adults. As you know, the internet offers a lot of
information, but not all of it is suitable for children and young adults. Parents have to be
aware of what their children are looking at on the internet and limit access to it so the
latter won’t have access to websites that contain strong and inappropriate language and
content. Moreover, many unethical communities or websites share content that exposes
children to situations, ideas, or materials that can upset and confuse them. This can lead
to misinformation or tempt children into dangerous situations or behaviours.
Second, the internet allows people to communicate and share information through social
media platforms. As long as you’re online and other people have your email or access to
your social media, they can harass or bully you. Finally, navigating through the internet

isn’t always safe. If you don’t take precautions to safeguard your online privacy, hackers
can access important personal information.
The internet has impacted our lives in many positive ways. Though it has several
drawbacks, its advantages far outweigh them, cementing its importance in our daily
lives.

The Sharing Economy
Look around at the things we have purchased at some point in our lives. (27)
Among the things are the smartphone that has been put away as we upgraded to the latest
model, the car that is only used on the weekends, and even the guest room in our house that
has somehow been turned into a storeroom. Those underused assets may appear useless to
some, yet they could be useful to others.
With the advent of the internet, online communities have discovered a method to
generate incomes from the sharing of underutilised assets. Websites and social media groups
are used to facilitate the buying and selling of second-hand goods. It is also now easier than
ever to engage in peer-to-peer sharing activities. (28)
The widespread use of online platforms presents opportunities for consumers to earn
quick money. For instance, working parents previously might have abandoned the idea of
selling their children’s outgrown clothes and old equipment. (29) However, online
marketplaces have made it easier for parents to sell unused items and put some cash back into
their pockets.
Businesses have also acknowledged the profitability of the sharing economy.
(30)_______A business model that is gaining popularity allows companies to provide digital
platforms which put customers in contact with individuals who can provide a particular
product or service. Companies like Airbnb act as a middleman for homeowners to cash in on
their unused rooms or houses by renting them out as accommodations. (31)
The shift towards a sharing economy is not without criticism. Unregulated
individuals, unlike corporations, are not required to obey certain regulations.(32)
Nevertheless, living in the consumer society at present, the greater chances to sell our
unwanted and underused goods could result in lower environmental impact which is
definitely advantageous to our overall well-being.
Adapted from: https://learnenglish.britishcouncil.org/skills/reading/b2-reading/sharing-economy

PART 5
[8 marks]
[Time suggested: Twenty minutes]
Questions 33 to 40 are based on the following texts. Read the texts carefully and answer the
questions that follow.
CULTURAL PRACTICES
A - Carlos, 21 years old
I love celebrating cultural festivals. For me, traditional dance and music are key elements.
They bring people together and foster a sense of community. Whether it’s a local festival or
a national celebration, participating in these events helps me stay connected to my roots.
Traditional costumes worn during these events also play a significant role in showcasing
our heritage.
B - Amina, 30 years old
Food is an integral part of our culture. Preparing and sharing traditional meals with family
and friends during festivals or special occasions is something I cherish. All the dishes tell
stories of our ancestors and can be a way to preserve our culinary heritage. I believe that
through food, we can connect with our culture on a deeper level.
C - Ravi, 25 years old
I think cultural rituals and ceremonies are important. They mark significant life events and
milestones. For instance, weddings, coming-of-age ceremonies, and festivals each have
their own set of rituals that are followed meticulously. These practices help in passing
down traditions from one generation to the next and keep our culture alive.
D - Mei, 28 years old
Art and craft are my favourite aspects of culture. I enjoy making traditional handicrafts and
learning about different art forms that are unique to my heritage. These activities are not
only creative but also help preserve the skills and techniques that have been passed down
through generations. It’s a way to express cultural identity and pride.
E - Ahmed, 35 years old
Language is a vital part of culture. Speaking and learning our native language helps us
maintain our cultural identity. It’s more than just a means of communication; it’s a way to
understand our history, literature, and traditions. Language connects us to our ancestors and
is crucial for cultural preservation.

F - Lila, 22 years old
Storytelling is a profound way to keep our culture alive. Folktales, myths, and legends
passed down orally from one generation to the next carry our collective wisdom and moral
values. Through stories, we can teach children about our culture, history, and traditions in
an engaging and memorable way.
